_comment: PREP-A-05: the leanest HoloOcean scenario that can serve as ArduSub SITL's external
physics backend. Loaded by holoocean_sitl_physics_host.py as a PLAIN scenario_cfg --
it deliberately does NOT go through scenario_manifest.load_realtime_manifest, whose
required-sensor validation exists for the perception loop and would force cameras and
sonar into a configuration whose whole point is that it has neither.
Why no cameras and no sonar: adapters/holoocean/docs/perf/tick_budget_2026-09-02.md
measured ~15 ms of fixed cost per tick with nothing rendering, plus ~65 ms per 1080p
camera frame and ~60 ms per 768x512 sonar frame. The SITL closed loop needs attitude,
depth and pose -- QGroundControl renders the vehicle, not the water -- so every
renderer is off and the tick budget goes entirely to physics. Perception is added back
later, on top of a loop that is already known to work, and pays the RTF cost then.
ticks_per_sec MUST equal the bridge's --step-hz and ArduPilot's SIM_RATE_HZ. One
HoloOcean tick advances HoloOcean's clock by 1/ticks_per_sec and the bridge advances
SITL's by 1/step_hz; any mismatch makes the two simulators' clocks drift apart while
each believes it is in sync. 50 Hz is chosen as the highest rate the ~15 ms/tick floor
can sustain at RTF ~1 with headroom for the WSL2<->Windows round trip.
frames_per_sec false = no wall-clock cap (the contract base pins 20, which is exactly
why round 1 of the tick budget measured 20 ticks/s regardless of GPU load).
Sensor set is deliberately minimal and only uses sensors this repo has already read
from a real install. If the installed HoloOcean exposes a DynamicsSensor, adding one
named 'DynamicsSensor' lets the bridge take velocity directly instead of differencing
PoseSensor (ardusub_sitl_bridge._extract_velocity handles both); it is left out here
so a first run cannot fail on an unrecognised sensor type.
name: uw_ardusub_sitl_bridge
